root_cause.text: The `i2c_imx_master_isr` interrupt handler unconditionally overwrites the `IMX_I2C_STATE_FAILED` state set by `i2c_imx_isr_read_block_data_len` with `IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_CONTINUE`, preventing proper error handling when invalid block read lengths are detected.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies `drivers/i2c/busses/i2c-imx.c` within `i2c_imx_master_isr` by wrapping the state assignment `i2c_imx->state = IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_CONTINUE;` with a condition `if (i2c_imx->state == IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_BLOCK_DATA_LEN)`, ensuring that error states set by the length handler are preserved rather than overwritten.

intent_record.how: Prevents overwriting the driver state with an outdated transition target if the state has already changed due to concurrent interrupt handling or internal modifications within the helper function.

candidates.rationale: This statement unconditionally assigns IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_CONTINUE to the state variable, overwriting any IMX_I2C_STATE_FAILED status that may have been set by the preceding function call i2c_imx_isr_read_block_data_len(). This prevents the driver from properly handling errors related to invalid block read lengths.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally assigns IMX_I2C_STATE_READ_CONTINUE to the state variable in the i2c_imx_master_isr interrupt handler. It overwrites any IMX_I2C_STATE_FAILED status that may have been set by the preceding function call i2c_imx_isr_read_block_data_len() when invalid block read lengths are detected. This prevents the driver from properly propagating error states, allowing the I2C transaction to continue incorrectly instead of failing gracefully.
